newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan August consumer prices up 5.05 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan August consumer prices up 5.05 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's August consumer prices rose 5.05 percent from a year earlier, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Thursday.
On a month-to-month basis, the August consumer price index was up 3.81 percent from July, the directorate said.
August wholesale prices were down 3.23 percent from August 1995 and up 0.63 percent from July 1996.
The August consumer price increase was the greatest monthly rise in more than a year since January 1995, when the consumer price index was 5.25 percent.
The agency attributed the sharp August uptick to price increases in the aftermath of two typhoons, Gloria and the far stronger Herb, that struck the island in late July and August.
"A sharp decrease in vegetable and fruit supplies caused vegetable prices to jump 89 percent and fruit prices 21 percent," the agency said in a statement.
"As there was no typhoon last year, the year-on-year figure expanded to 5.05 percent," it said.
The agency said that on a year-to-date basis, Taiwan's consumer price increase was a more muted 2.95 percent, still below the 1996 full-year target of 3.2 percent.
The target for second-half consumer price growth is 3.5 percent, the agency said.
